Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
A post-FOMC tape split between patience and dip-buying. iain is the skeptic and the loudest voice: 100% cash, two tiny losses since October 13, preaching that “sometimes the best trade is no trade at all” into a stack of software, cybersecurity, semis and earnings catalysts — and warning that traders would “rather lose money being early than make money being patient.” Enrich ran the busiest board again: a 10/29 watchlist (SKHY, PLTR, MSTR, RKLB, TSLA, NBIS, SHOP) with the list-wide note to watch for buyers near the daily 9 EMA / support, a SHOP bull-flag call with a $169 line, a puts-ready downside note, and PCE as the morning's line of defense. Prof is the dip-buyer and the victory-lapper: GOOGL's dip to $288 is “an attractive price” on a mega cap at a 30% discount (while doubting the retail dip-buy), and LITE's $200 move is a completed call he shared live. Venu supplied the discipline: the 3-Day Rule for post-earnings gaps, aimed squarely at GOOGL and MSFT. DiCarlo supplied the extremes: VRT up 30%+ since his zone, HIMS expected +40% in 90 days out of compression, ENPH down 35%+ and near his stop, META pulling into a buy zone whose level is in his video. Sean posted no ticker call — only his swing-challenge day 2 and a biotech/healthcare breakout observation. Remz posted no ticker call either — only FOMC-day composure and a vague “wait until next week.” Your process sides with the watchers: the closest thing to a qualifier shape is SHOP's bull flag 0.46% from its trigger, with RKLB's $59 gap-fill 0.68% away as the second-nearest live level; everything else is a paid or extended move (NBIS, VRT, LITE), a gap to let settle for three days (GOOGL, MSFT), a retest to hold (TSLA), or a watchlist mention with no level (SKHY, PLTR, MSTR).

From the group

Sean — no ticker calls, only the challenge and a sector note: day 2 of his free 3-day swing-trading challenge (“Learning how to enter and exit trades with absolute precision”), plus: “A lot of biotech and healthcare names are continuing to push higher and break out right now… Even though the broader market has been choppy, there have still been plenty of opportunities if you're looking at the right sectors and the right stocks.” No biotech ticker is named, so no row follows from it.

iain — process posts: “Been cash heavy the last 2 weeks, taken exactly 2 trades since October 13th (both tiny Ls), and have been sitting on my bum ever since” (Oct 27) — the setup for his 100%-cash stance above; plus a 20-minute scanning routine that starts with a market check on $SPY, $QQQ, $IWM and $VIX, and a pullback-buying note (“buying pullbacks in leading names in leading groups as they turned back up off the moving averages”) as his most rewarding 2026 improvement.

Remz — composure, no tickers: “If you didn't tilt on FOMC day you're probably gonna make it” and “Guys, the fun hasn't even started yet. Just wait until we get through next week lmao. I genuinely think we're in for some crazy shit. Do your best to stay open minded for now.” No ticker, no level — so Remz has no row today, for the first time in this run's recent editions.

Venu — the 3-Day Rule, in full: “Before you rush to buy a stock that's down 15-20% after earnings, understand one important rule: The 3-Day Rule! When a stock gaps down sharply after earnings or bad news, wait at least 3 trading days before…” — quoted to the visible cutoff. The rule is applied to GOOGL and MSFT in their panels above. His Oct 28 earnings preview (GOOGL, MSFT, NOW reporting after the bell, with AI CapEx the metric to watch) is context for both panels; NOW itself gets no row, since no call on it followed.

DiCarlo — levels live in videos, not posts: all four of his window posts point to videos: VRT targets/stops for the continuation, META's buy-zone level plus target/stop/timeline, ENPH's risk management from his stop, and HIMS's target/stop/timeline. Where a level is not in the visible post, this feed quotes none rather than guessing from a video title. His SMH/BTC cycle posts from yesterday are not repeated today.

Prof — earnings scoreboard: “$MSFT Ramped +4.1% / $GOOGL Tanked -7.8%. What a day.” Both figures are after-hours prints reported by Prof, not Yahoo regular-session closes — the panels above keep them labeled as such, and all distances in this feed use the regular close.

Sources & Methodology
  • Accounts scanned (7): Sean trades @SRxTrades · iain @ohiain · Enrich Trades @enrichtrades · Remz @Remzztrades · Prof @TheProfInvestor · Venu @Venu_7_ · Peter DiCarlo @pdicarlotrader. Sean and Remz posted no new ticker call in this window, so neither has a row — readability is not the constraint, content is.
  • Posts window: Wed Oct 28 – Thu Oct 29, 2026 — everything visible after the Oct 28 feed's window (which ended Oct 28, ~11:45 UTC). Logged-out X shows only the ~5 most recent posts per account; posts truncated in the extraction itself (Prof's GOOGL dip post, Venu's 3-Day Rule post, Sean's biotech post, iain's catalyst post) are quoted only to the visible cutoff. Where a post is truncated, the feed says so instead of guessing the rest.
  • Price data: Yahoo Finance daily data, as of the Wed Oct 28, 2026 close — this run is pre-market Thursday, so Wednesday's close is the latest completed close and Thursday's session is not in any number here. Moves described as “after hours” (Prof's MSFT +4.1% and GOOGL -7.8%, and the GOOGL dip toward $288) happened after that close and are reported as the trader's figures, with no price invented for them; every distance-to-trigger in this feed uses the regular close. Trader-stated = a level or call from their post, attributed by name. Chart check = computed by us from that data — it can confirm or push back on a trader's framing, and it's labeled every time.
  • Sector lines: each card's sector/industry ETF comparison (Yahoo Finance, Wed Oct 28, 2026 close) — close, day change, Weinstein stage by the same 30-week MA method, and price vs the 50-week EMA. Mappings: AAPL/VRT/LITE\u2192XLK, MSFT/PLTR/SHOP\u2192IGV, NVDA\u2192SMH, GOOGL/META\u2192XLC, AMZN/TSLA\u2192XLY, NBIS\u2192CLOU (cloud computing \u2014 best fit), RKLB\u2192UFO (space \u2014 best fit), SKHY\u2192EWY (South Korea \u2014 best fit for the KOSPI name), MSTR\u2192IBIT (spot bitcoin \u2014 best fit; a bitcoin-treasury proxy), HIMS\u2192XLV (health care \u2014 best fit), ENPH\u2192ICLN (clean energy \u2014 best fit). Best-fit choices are noted here, not hidden.
  • Where none of the seven commented, the section says Unavailable / no trader signal — never “unchanged.” All four indexes are unavailable this window: no trader posted an index-specific level or trade call (the SPY panel carries iain's cash stance and Enrich's puts note as context, and the QQQ panel carries iain's market-check mention, but none names an index level, so the strip labels stay unavailable).
  • Qualifier rules (constructive pullback into a key MA/support, tightening base near highs, confirmed breakout; never extended/chased). Closest qualifier shape, not yet fired: SHOP (bull flag at all-time highs, trigger 0.46% away) — the only green chip with a live trigger this close. Constructive holds, not entries: PLTR, AAPL (holds-only at the highs). Gap watches under the 3-day rule: GOOGL, MSFT. Retest / gap-fill watches: TSLA ($400 retest), RKLB ($59 gap fill, 0.68% away). Thesis watches, no level: META (buy zone in video), HIMS (compression into earnings), SKHY (big day, no trend read). Watchlist mentions, no level: PLTR, MSTR. Paid or extended moves, not entries: NBIS (paid 50%+), VRT (+30% run), LITE ($200 move). Broken: ENPH (down 35%+, near its stop). Chart checks only: NVDA, AMZN.
  • Coverage note: nothing is carried over silently. Yesterday's ideas appear here only where today's posts repeat them (SKHY, PLTR, RKLB, TSLA) — and then only under today's calls, which sometimes differ from yesterday's (RKLB's $59 target is still unhit; TSLA's $400 break is now a retest). FSLY, MRVL, SNDK, DELL, MU, AMD, AVGO, NOW, KO, WDC, STX, HOOD, NXPI, CIFR, ALAB and the rest of yesterday's board are not rows because today's posts do not repeat those calls.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt. SKHY carries a “No 30-wk history” pill instead of a stage: too few weekly closes exist for a 30-week MA or 50-week EMA yet.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2\u20133 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition. Media URLs exist in the logged-out profile HTML, but they could not be reliably matched to specific posts (the same reason no trader chart was embedded on Oct 26\u201328), so no trader chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line's endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built \u2014 all 63 computable lines passed within 0.5%. The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only. SKHY's 30-week MA and 50-week EMA are not applicable (insufficient history) and are shown as such, not estimated.
